source: docs/L7V2_DESIGN.md sections 4, 5, 7, 12 and 13 (approved 2026-10-30 as recommended, D-V1..D-V10; TPC-W v1.8 as the benign navigation source); the T-018 review's mapping rules (2026-10-30)
rule: The traffic side of L7 v2, frozen before any L7 v2 or P3 capture (design section 13 items 3 and 4, the harm admission rule). A change is a new file version, labelled post hoc in the design's 'As built' section; tests/test_l7v2_prereg.py pins every value. Every value marked ASSUMPTION is declared, not measured.

navigation.model: TPC-W v1.8 clause 5.2.2.4 Threshold tables (ml/tpcw_v18.json); next interaction by rule 5.2.2.3
navigation.unused_note: Ordering is not emulated: 49.5 % of its interactions have no route, and no order-flow mapping is frozen (T-018 F13)
navigation.iid_zipf_note: today's i.i.d. Zipf page model (ml/l7_benign.browser_views) stays as an additional held-out benign kind
navigation.session_model: in-session navigation for the whole run; the User Session Minimum Duration (15 min) is not emulated
navigation.unmapped_rule: watched chain: a step into an unmapped state emits no request and takes no time; the next emitted interaction is the next mapped state the chain reaches
mapping_notes: Search Request is the page that carries the form, a C1 page view; only Search Results runs the query (T-018 F10, F12)
the Order group is not mapped to /export; only Order Display (it 'displays the status of the last order') is, as an in-page C5 request
Order Inquiry ('enter or confirm their identity') is a form page, like Search Request [DEVIATION from T-018 F11's approximate row, which put it on /export too]
navigation.referer: a page request carries the previous document of the device (none at session entry); its assets and its in-page requests carry their document
navigation.cookies: every client keeps the cookies the server sets (one requests.Session per device)

search_terms.note: the same function for benign search users and for the bots (C2: 'search terms drawn like the benign search users'')

export_r.note: r changes only the URL's work factor (bench/origin.py)

search_user.model: a browser device: Home, then the search page; each search is in-page from the search page; after a search, a product page with probability p_detail, then back to the search page; otherwise the next search
search_user.p_detail_source: TPC-W v1.8 browsing mix, Search Results -> Product Detail (threshold 9868 - 3674)
search_user.status: ASSUMPTION (no measured source, T-012 G3 gap)

exporter.model: a browser device: visits separated by a uniform gap; a visit loads the account page, waits a think time, then requests one export in-page
exporter.status: ASSUMPTION (no measured source, T-012 G3 gap)

flash_crowd.model: new TPC-W browsing devices (one address each) whose first view falls within the first 60 s of their slot
flash_crowd.grounding: [G3-06-Q1]: in a flash crowd, per-client rates drop; so no client here is faster than an ordinary device

C2.name: request-cost abuse
C2.intensity: level L of the spare capacity S (bench/calibration.spare_capacity of the record in use)
C2.ua: one browser UA per source, drawn from ml/l7_benign.UA_TABLE by weight
C2.referer: the page that carries the route's form (/page/search for C3, /page/account for C5), never loaded by the bot

C3a.name: browser-claiming HTTP-library bots
C3a.costly: one costly request right after each page
C3a.intensity: level L of S, carried by the number of sources n = ceil(L * S / ((cost_C1 + cost_route) / 1000 / mean(page_gap_s)))
C3a.out_of_bounds: a level whose n falls outside the bounds is not run; the ladder reports it as not reachable
C3a.referer: page requests carry the previous page (none for the first); the costly request carries its page

C3b.name: headless-browser bots, non-human navigation (a request-level emulation)
C3b.costly: each navigation view is followed by the form page of its costly route (/page/search for C3, /page/account for C5; a page view whose Referer is the navigation page) and then by one costly request issued in-page from that form page (Referer: the form page); every step waits a dwell from the mimicry law, so the costly request comes a dwell after its form page, as a benign search or export does
C3b.costly_label: re-registered 2026-10-31 by the user, before any capture (T-030 L7V2-04: no Referer or timing tell; C2 and C3a, the controls, keep theirs). When 05176fc wrote this label the user had not yet decided: it was a forward reference, confirmed by the user on 2026-10-31 (C3b: 'Keep, aim at export')
C3b.route_label: re-registered 2026-10-31 by the user, before any capture: C3b's costly route is export (C5), search (C3) the variant (the user's 'Keep, aim at export'); its form page is the account page that benign exporters load
C3b.ladder_note: if 300 bots cannot be carried (the ~300-alias limit with the benign population), the ladder stops at 200 and the knee is searched below it
C3b.assets: waves and a cache like a browser device, 6 keep-alive connections
C3b.referer: like the benign browser: the previous page for a page, the page for its assets, the form page for the costly request

M1.pages: product pages, uniform without replacement (deep links)

M2.pages: product pages, uniform without replacement (deep links)

M3.pages: the TPC-W browsing chain watched on its page states (Home, Product Detail, New Products, Best Sellers, Search Request, Order Inquiry); product pages uniform without replacement (no back-navigation)

mimicry.exhausted: when every product page has been visited, a new uniform permutation starts
mimicry.rule: the values are ASSUMPTIONS fixed here, before any model sees data; they are never adjusted after a model has been scored; the harm ladder may change only the number of bots

arrivals.label: re-registered 2026-10-31 by the user, before any capture (T-030 L7V2-03; the user's 'L7v2 fixes: approve both')
arrivals.benign: every benign entity, in every role, arrives at a time drawn uniformly over [0, the last attack slot's end - min_active_s] and runs to the capture's end; a CGNAT pool runs from 0 and each of its users arrives over the same span; held-out kinds arrive like the trained ones, with no slot
arrivals.attack: every attack entity arrives at a time drawn uniformly over [its slot's start, its slot's end - min_active_s] and runs to its slot's end
arrivals.flash_crowd: its arrival window (arrive_within_s) starts at a time drawn uniformly over the benign arrival span, at least flash_gap_s away from every attack slot's start

lifetimes.label: re-registered 2026-10-31 under D-034 (the user's 'Approve all three', 2026-10-31T12:10:57Z), before any capture (review T-038, finding T038-01: arrivals were matched, but key lifetimes still coded the role)
lifetimes.law_status: ASSUMPTION: no measured session-length source in the T-012 corpus; the floor is min_active_s; the ceiling is above the 240 s slot, so a share of the keys of either role outlives one slot
lifetimes.benign: a benign key is a session: an L7 v2 browser-like kind (tpcw_browsing, tpcw_shopping, zipf_browser, search_user, exporter, flash_crowd, and each user of a CGNAT pool) runs, from its first view, sessions whose lifetimes are drawn from the law, separated by a gap drawn uniformly over gap_s, while at least min_left_s of its run remain (always one); every session starts with a fresh browser state (no cookies, so a new sid, and an empty cache), so a returning user is a new key; the entity, its address, its UA and its budget units are unchanged
lifetimes.machine_clients: a benign entity whose generator has no sessions (the polite crawler, api_bulk and the P5 kinds) runs one lifetime drawn from the law from its arrival, capped at the capture's end
lifetimes.attack: every attack entity runs one lifetime drawn from the law from its arrival (the arrival rule above is unchanged), capped at the capture's end, so it may stay active past its slot's end into the next slot
lifetimes.reuse: an M3 bot reuses the address of a trained attack entity that has stopped before the M3 bot starts and whose address no other M3 bot uses: C2 entities first, then the other trained families, in plan order

age_check.statistic: the first-seen times (seconds from the capture start) of the key units: an entity's arrival, and each CGNAT user's first view; the flash crowd is left out, being a burst by definition
age_check.rule: an l7v2 plan is refused unless the two-sample KS distance between the benign and the attack first-seen times is at most ks_max, the AUC of first-seen time as a score for the attack role is within 0.5 +- auc_band, and, when it holds held-out benign kinds, their KS distance to the trained benign kinds' is at most held_out_ks_max
age_check.label_v2: extended 2026-10-31 under D-034, before any capture (T038-01): key lifetimes and window age join the first-seen check above, which is unchanged
age_check.key_units_v2: a key unit is one key of the plan replayed at nominal times: each plan user of a benign entity (a session, or a machine client's one lifetime) and each attack entity; a P5 kind without a plan is one unit over its schedule and has no windows
age_check.window_rule: the trainer's view windows at nominal times (docs/L7V2_DESIGN.md 8.1 and section 16): a page request (route class C1) opens a token, a later non-page request joins the open token, a request before the unit's first page is a pageless token; one window per token j >= min_views of a unit; its age is the nominal start of token j minus that of the unit's first token
age_check.rule_v2: an l7v2 plan is also refused unless (a) the lifetimes (the nominal start of a unit's last request minus that of its first) of the trained benign and the trained attack key units have a KS distance of at most lifetime_ks_max and an AUC, lifetime as a score for the attack role, within 0.5 +- lifetime_auc_band; (b) window age as a score for the attack role has an AUC within 0.5 +- window_age_auc_band for the trained attack windows pooled, and for the windows of every attack family with at least family_min_units key units (held-out families included), each against the trained benign windows; (c) when the plan holds held-out benign kinds, the KS distance of their lifetimes to the trained benign kinds' is at most held_out_lifetime_ks_max

harm.metric: request-level Q and p95 of the benign clients against the calibration record's slo_ms, on its judged_profiles, with eval/harm_gate.py's rules unchanged (criterion, floors, control health, 1-s bins)
harm.never_sent_rule: every planned view, and every paced request, is judged against the device's own closed-loop schedule: its intended start is the completion of the device's previous view (or request) plus that one's pause (or gap), the first one's is its nominal start, and a view that never completed hands its intended start on. A view whose intended start falls in the attack window and that did not start within never_sent_after_s of it counts every request it planned as failed (err never_sent) at t_intended = that intended start; a started view's planned requests without a row count the same way. One stall therefore fails only the views that were slow, and a paced kind's own latency books no failure
harm.never_sent_label: re-registered 2026-10-31 by the user, before any capture (T-030 L7V2-01, L7V2-02; the user's 'L7v2 fixes: approve both')
harm.admission: class k enters the P1 verdicts only if U_k passes the harm gate's criterion against C over at least min_blocks valid blocks (dQ or dL), its placebo C' does not pass, and the calibration record is frozen; otherwise its verdict is V-D 'no harm'. Nothing is retuned after admission

cross_check.rule: a block is invalid as a client-side artefact when its client-side dQ >= 10 pp but the server-side Q(U), from nginx's $request_time for the same benign entities, is >= 99 %

ladder.knee: bench/calibration.knee: the lowest level whose harm reaches the floor in both repeats

harm.verdict_record: only a frozen calibration record; a placeholder or a measured record is refused
